channel.title: Acme: Tech News
channel.description: Articles about software, publishing and the open web.

item.title: WordPress 7.2 introduces a standard Secrets API
item.description: WordPress 7.2 will give core, plugins and hosts a common way to store credentials encrypted at rest. The API supports rotation, versioned values and a host-provided drop-in, while self-hosted installations must define WP_SECRETS_KEY before secrets can be saved.

item.title: The Bulwark and Vox Media form broad current-affairs partnership
item.description: Vox Media will handle advertising, podcast hosting and cross-promotion for The Bulwark under a partnership promising nearly 200 hours of current-affairs programming each month in 2027. The deal joins a growing independent political newsroom with Vox’s distribution and sales infrastructure.

item.title: Atmosphere cooperative organizes builders around the open social web
item.description: Developers, organizers and artists have launched the Atmosphere Community Cooperative to build shared tools, services and community around AT Protocol. Its member-governed structure is an experiment in giving the people who create an interoperable social ecosystem a direct stake in its direction.

item.title: Podnews maps podcast apps by open feature support
item.description: Podnews updated its searchable catalog of newer podcast apps, with filters for transcripts, chapters, funding, location, alternate enclosures, people and value payments. The list makes it easier to see which players implement Podcasting 2.0 features across mobile, desktop and the web.

item.title: WordPress 7.2 adds random discovery across posts and archives
item.description: WordPress 7.2 will add a /random/ route that redirects visitors to a random published post and can also work inside category and author archives. Site owners can customize the base, exclude post types or disable the feature, creating a built-in path back into older writing.

item.title: Raj Shamani’s Figuring Out passes 22 million subscribers
item.description: Podnews reports that Figuring Out with Raj Shamani has reached 22.1 million YouTube subscribers, moving ahead of The Diary of a CEO and The Joe Rogan Experience. The India-based show launched in 2021, a striking shift in the global center of gravity for creator-led podcast video.

item.title: Reprint copies a live WordPress site into a portable local workspace
item.description: WordPress introduced Reprint, a free open-source PHP tool that copies a site’s database and files over HTTP to a laptop, development server or new host. It can pull a live site into WordPress Playground in the browser, providing a practical migration, debugging and staging path without depending on a host-specific transfer system.

item.title: Journalism groups cancel conferences as event economics deteriorate
item.description: Nieman Lab reports that the Online News Association, OpenNews and other journalism groups are canceling conferences or cutting staff as travel, venue and production costs rise while grants shrink. Events once provided major revenue and professional ties, making the retreat another sign of weakening infrastructure around independent newsrooms.

item.title: San Jose Earthquakes pass from John Fisher to Alden co-founder Heath Freeman
item.description: Heath Freeman, a founding member and president of Alden Global Capital, will acquire the Earthquakes and PayPal Park from John Fisher and partners. MLS governors approved the transfer, expected to close within weeks. The reported $625 million valuation ends nearly two decades of Fisher ownership and gives San Jose a new local sports power center.

item.title: Molly Webster becomes a co-host of Radiolab
item.description: Longtime producer Molly Webster will join Latif Nasser as co-host of Radiolab, succeeding Lulu Miller as the public-radio show approaches its 25th anniversary. Webster has worked on the program since 2012 and created its Gonads and Breathe series. Miller will concentrate on the family-oriented spinoff Terrestrials.

item.title: Indonesia considers making platforms pay for news aggregation
item.description: A proposed Indonesian copyright bill would require large platforms to compensate publishers when aggregating news or displaying previews and snippets. With more than 230 million internet users, Indonesia could become Southeast Asia’s first country with such a regime. Critics question the state-run payment system and permit sanctions.

item.title: iHeart denies a report that it plans to sell its podcast division
item.description: Bloomberg reported that iHeartMedia was exploring a sale of part or all of its podcast operation, but the company said it has no such plan. The division produced $174 million in third-quarter revenue, up 24.6 percent. CEO Bob Pittman says iHeart will begin reporting podcast results separately so investors can better see the unit’s value.

item.title: A personal blog can serve its writer before it serves an audience
item.description: Bob Dunn argues that a blog need not chase reach or polish every entry into an essay. Quick thoughts, links and photos can build a durable personal archive on a site the writer controls, creating value even when nobody else reads a post. It is a crisp case for publishing on your own domain.

item.title: Former Ringer producers launch a podcast about how the web used to feel
item.description: Bobby Wagner and Alex Bazeley’s independent Click Through turns Wikipedia racing into a weekly show: start at two unrelated pages and navigate between them using only links. Recorded around New York, it treats Wikipedia, websites and digressive browsing as an antidote to platform-controlled discovery.

item.title: WordCamp Asia 2027 heads to Penang with a $35 ticket
item.description: The WordPress community will gather April 9–11 at Penang’s waterfront convention center for Contributor Day and two conference days. The 2026 edition drew 2,627 people and more than 1,500 contributors; registration for the 2027 Contributor Day opens Jan. 27 and is capped at 600.
